description.short: Downy green tea from Mount Huangshan, fresh and delicate with subtle floral orchid notes
description.overview: Grown in the misty Huangshan mountains, a celebrated UNESCO World Heritage site. Constant mountain mist and high humidity create a gentle microclimate that slows leaf growth, concentrating rich amino acids and aromatic compounds.
description.leaf: Delicately twisted bud-and-leaf sets ('sparrow tongues'), covered in fine white down, with a characteristic golden fish-tail tip at the base
description.aroma: Fresh, delicate orchid floral notes with nuances of sweet spring meadow
description.taste: Mild, clean, and subtly sweet without astringency, carrying faint orchid undertones
description.processing: Plucking of one bud with one leaf → brief withering → wok fixation → gentle rolling/shaping → multi-stage low-temperature drying and baking

history.origin: The name means 'Yellow Mountain Fur Peak' — referencing the fine downy fuzz covering the tender young shoots and its birthplace in the Yellow Mountains
history.development: First crafted in the late 19th century by local tea merchants adapting traditional pan-firing methods to the unique mountain terroir of Huangshan
history.modern: Recognized as one of China's Ten Famous Teas and an iconic agricultural treasure of Anhui Province
interestingFacts: Mount Huangshan is a UNESCO World Heritage site, where terraced tea gardens thrive alongside ancient granite peaks and pine forests
The highest grade is hand-picked during a very narrow window of just a few days in early spring, accounting for its scarcity and premium status
